prompt.context: Your client, ValueCenter, is the nation's largest, global retailer. The company is implementing a new supplier management system in order to increase the transparency into the purchasing decisions and ultimately decrease costs. This new system will replace thousands of homegrown systems currently used within the company. Currently, orders placed from suppliers are manually keyed into ValueCenter's ERP system at local offices by employees. With the new system, the goal is to have a centralized platform where ValueCenter employees can input new supplier information and place orders. Additionally, the new system will allow suppliers to log into the system to update information like address and billing changes, something ValueCenter employees had to do in the past. Because of the size and international scope of ValueCenter, the implementation of the system will be rolled out in phases. The leadership at ValueCenter is worried about how this change will affect its employees and productivity so has hired you to advise the company through this change.
prompt.question: How would you assist the client as it goes through this large-scale change?

clarifying_info.q: Has ValueCenter gone through a large-scale technology implementation before?
clarifying_info.a: Yes. The last large-scale tech implementation resulted in a huge loss in productivity because of a lack of training. Because of this, training is a priority for leadership.

clarifying_info.q: Which markets will be included in the initial rollout?
clarifying_info.a: Leadership wants to roll out the implementation in mid-size markets first. Proposed markets are Mexico, Hong Kong, Brazil, and Canada.

clarifying_info.q: Are there any constraints around the training approach?
clarifying_info.a: Management needs the training schedule to be flexible and time-sensitive. Hours spent in training are hours spent away from productive work.

clarifying_info.q: What is the company culture like?
clarifying_info.a: The culture of ValueCenter is high efficiency at the lowest possible cost.

framework: Assess — understand the current state, identify stakeholders, and document change impacts
Design — develop training materials, a communications plan, and a Change Agent Network
Deliver — execute training close to Go-Live, roll out phased communications, and activate change agents

questions.prompt: Who are the key stakeholders involved in this change, and how should ValueCenter approach them?
questions.guidance: Strong answers identify multiple stakeholder groups: employees who manually key orders into the ERP at local offices, local office management, IT/system owners, suppliers who will gain self-service access, and corporate leadership. Candidate should note that stakeholder salience varies by location and role, and that a formal stakeholder analysis should map impact level to each group.

questions.prompt: What anticipated challenges do you foresee with this implementation?
questions.guidance: Strong answers surface: resistance to change from employees whose tasks are being automated or changed; risk of productivity loss (as happened in the prior implementation) if training is inadequate; language and cultural barriers across Mexico, Hong Kong, Brazil, and Canada; time-zone coordination; variation in existing homegrown systems that the new platform must replace; supplier adoption of the self-service portal; maintaining day-to-day operations during rollout.

questions.prompt: Walk through the phases you would propose for the implementation rollout.
questions.guidance: Excellent candidates structure around Assess → Design → Deliver. Under Assess: conduct a stakeholder analysis to identify impacted employees at each target location; run a change impact assessment (forums with impacted stakeholders) to surface concerns and document all procedural changes that will need training or communications. Under Design: build training materials in multiple formats (instructor-led, computer-based, quick-reference/FAQ guides) to accommodate all learning styles and keep time away from work minimal; create a communications plan specifying audience, message, frequency, channel, and due date; establish a Change Agent Network of champion employees who receive additional system training and serve as on-the-ground SMEs for colleagues. Under Deliver: roll out training as close to the Go-Live date as possible to maximize retention while minimising lost productivity; execute phased communications — early messages build awareness, later messages become tactical with specific system guidance and Go-Live preparation steps; facilitate Change Agent Network meetings to keep agents informed; communicate to all employees that change agents are the go-to resource so management can maintain day-to-day activity.

brainstorming.prompt: What workstreams would you prioritise and how would you tailor the approach given ValueCenter's culture of high efficiency at the lowest possible cost?

categories.name: Training
ideas: Prioritise computer-based training and quick-reference guides over lengthy instructor-led sessions to minimise time away from work
Schedule training as close to Go-Live as possible to reduce re-learning
Leverage change agents to deliver peer training at low cost
Create modular, role-specific training content so employees only learn what is relevant to them

categories.name: Communications
ideas: Use existing internal channels (email, intranet) to keep communication costs low
Segment messaging by stakeholder group and location to avoid information overload
Start with awareness-building messages early; shift to tactical how-to guidance as Go-Live nears
Provide supplier-facing communications explaining new self-service capabilities

categories.name: Change Management
ideas: Build a Change Agent Network from existing high-performing employees to avoid external consulting costs
Hold structured Change Agent meetings on a regular cadence pre-Go-Live
Empower change agents to handle frontline questions so management bandwidth is preserved
Tie change agent participation to recognition or career development incentives

categories.name: Phasing & Risk Mitigation
ideas: Pilot in one mid-size market before full four-country rollout to identify issues early
Define clear rollback or contingency procedures if the Go-Live encounters problems
Establish productivity KPIs to monitor impact during and after cutover
Capture lessons learned after each market Go-Live and incorporate them into subsequent phases

recommendation: Adopt an Assess-Design-Deliver change management approach, with training as the top priority given the productivity loss in the prior implementation
Roll out in phases starting with mid-size markets (Mexico, Hong Kong, Brazil, Canada), piloting in one country first to de-risk subsequent launches
Establish a Change Agent Network to maximise grassroots adoption while minimising cost and management bandwidth requirements
risks: Productivity dip during transition if training is insufficient or timed too far ahead of Go-Live
Employee resistance in markets with cultural or language barriers
Supplier non-adoption of the new self-service portal, requiring continued manual support
Budget overrun if instructor-led training is over-relied upon across four international markets
next_steps: Conduct stakeholder analysis and change impact assessment for each target market immediately
Define training format mix and build materials; identify and onboard change agents
Establish Go-Live dates and work backward to set training and communications milestones for each market
